Transcript body:
[00:00] Avery (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making the time. Quick roll call and then we'll move into the kickoff agenda. I'm Avery Chen, AE on the account, joined by Miguel from our SE team.
[00:12] Tom (CTO): Tom here, hi.
[00:14] Priya (Infra): Priya on infra side.
[00:16] Derek (DevOps): Derek.
[00:18] Miguel (SE): Miguel, thanks Tom, Priya, Derek.
[00:20] Avery: Alright, real quick — objective today's to align on pilot scope, security check points, and next steps so we can get a pilot environment spun up in the next two weeks. Sound good?
[00:29] Priya: Yes that's right. We have a compliance window we need to respect — SOC2 evidence, SAML SSO, and we need to validate KMS integration for key wraps.
[00:37] Avery: Good, we'll cover those. Miguel, do you want to run through the typical pilot patterns we see?
[00:42] Miguel: Sure. Most customers run a two-week pilot: week one is connectivity and small functional tests, week two is performance and quality benchmarks. For Crestline's use case — triage notes and clinical-summarization pipelines — we usually recommend starting on Redwood Hosted to get baseline metrics, then evaluate Dedicated if you need guaranteed throughput or on-prem for data residency.
[01:05] Tom: We're leaning toward a Dedicated pool down the road but for pilot we'd prefer hosted to move faster. The big ask is that any PHI doesn't persist in logs and we need to understand retention.
[01:16] Avery: Understood. We can do hosted with stricter retention and audit log controls. We'll share our security pack. I noted SOC2 and at-rest/in-transit encryption with KMS — Miguel can cover the exact fields we can toggle.
[01:30] Miguel: For hosted, we offer customer-managed KMS via cloud KMS integrations, and audit logs are available for export. Note: in some transcripts I've seen "K-V cash" misread but it's KV cache — we can evict KV caches on teardown if you want non-persistent state.
[01:48] Priya: Evicting KV cache on teardown sounds good. We also need SSO — SAML — and RBAC controls mapped to our Okta groups.
[01:56] Avery: SAML is supported; we have role mappings and can pre-provision team roles from Okta groups. We'll include the SSO flow in the runbook.
[02:04] Derek: Networking question — do you prefer VPC peering or do you support private link? Our security team typically only allows peering and tight egress rules.
[02:13] Miguel: We support both; for Hosted we typically use VPC peering. For Dedicated or Private deployments we can provision a VPC with peering, or an on-prem package if you need air-gapped. For the pilot, peering will be simplest.
[02:26] Tom: Great. Timeline wise, we'd like a pilot ready before the end of the month — that gives our data team time to run it against masked records.
[02:34] Avery: Two-week pilot starting next Monday is feasible if we get the infra artifacts this week. Derek, can you share cluster diagrams and expected QPS?
[02:44] Derek: Yes I can, I'll send that today. We have a k8s cluster with three node pools and expect about 20 req/s peak for the pilot, mostly 256–512 token responses but some longer threads.
[02:57] Miguel: Good to know. For 20 QPS with 512 tokens most customers either configure moderate batching and a cold-start tuning profile or move to a dedicated pool if you need lower tail latencies. We'll recommend quantization only after we validate output quality.
[03:13] Priya: On data residency — some flows must remain within the EU. We have a couple of EU-only pipelines. Can Redwood host the pilot in eu-west?
[03:22] Avery: Yes, we have eu-west regions. We'll note region-specific deploys and data residency controls in the runbook.
[03:29] Tom: Perfect. Security-wise, we'll need the SOC2 attestation and a document on your penetration testing cadence.
[03:35] Avery: I'll upload our security pack which includes SOC2, penetration test summaries, and our encryption docs. That's one of the next steps.
[03:45] Miguel: Also we'll include recommended firewall rules and sample terraform snippets for peering to make the network work as frictionless as possible.
[03:53] Derek: On logging, are there token-level cost breakdowns sent anywhere? We want to map cost back to feature flags.
[03:59] Miguel: We have token-level usage exports and per-route dashboards in the Console. We'll show how to instrument routes and cost tags during the SE deep-dive.
[04:10] Tom: Speaking of deep-dive, can we do a focused session on performance — latency SLOs, cold-start, warm pools?
[04:16] Miguel: Absolutely. We'll run a 60–90 minute session and include a bench plan: synthetic QPS patterns, 99th percentile tail, and a comparison of hosted with and without batching.
[04:28] Avery: I'll coordinate scheduling. Prefer morning PST or early EU friendly slot?
[04:33] Tom: Morning PST works for us.
[04:35] Avery: Noted.
[04:37] Miguel: Quick note on canary and rollouts — once you hit production, you can route a subset of traffic to different model variants, or fallback to a smaller model during degraded capacity. That gives you graceful degradation if Dedicated hits limits.
[04:50] Priya: We'll want that — automatic fallback is a big win. Also, is there an option to pin model versions to the pipeline? We need reproducible outputs for audit.
[04:58] Miguel: Yes, version pinning is supported; you can lock to a specific model and we can snapshot prompts and their evals. We also have rollouts and A/B testing features in the Console.
[05:10] Derek: Practically, what do you need from us this week to kick off?
[05:14] Avery: 1) infra diagram and QPS (Derek). 2) list of PII-bearing flows and retention requirements (Tom). 3) contact for Okta SSO onboarding (Priya). 4) preferred peering windows and firewall contacts (Priya/Derek). If we get those, Miguel and I can turn up the pilot in ~5 business days.
[05:31] Tom: Okay we'll try to send everything by EOD tomorrow.
[05:35] Priya: We'll coordinate internally and share SSO contact.
[05:38] Miguel: For the bench, small heads-up: the first run is often noisy because of caching and kv-cache warmups — we recommend at least three runs and a teardown between to capture consistent cold-starts.
[05:50] Tom: Makes sense. On metrics, we'll want 50th/95th/99th latency, token counts, and cost per 1k tokens.
[05:58] Avery: We'll include those in the bench template.
[06:01] [brief pause]
[06:05] Miguel: One more question about data — do you plan to send raw PHI to the model or will it be pre-masked?
[06:11] Tom: For pilot we'll use masked but realistic records. Long-term we need to evaluate end-to-end PHI handling and an eventual Private deployment.
[06:20] Avery: Understood. We'll treat pilot as masked flows for now and plan for a compliance review as a follow-up if you want Private later.
[06:28] Priya: Any cost estimates for expected pilot? We need a ballpark for budget holder.
[06:33] Miguel: For a two-week hosted pilot at 20 QPS and average 400 tokens per request, rough estimate — we can run numbers after we get more exact token distributions. We'll send an initial cost sheet.
[06:46] Derek: Good.
[06:48] Avery: Okay, let's quickly recap next steps before we run out of time. Miguel: what do you need to prep?
[06:53] Miguel: I'll draft the bench plan and provide terraform snippets and network checklist. Will schedule the 60-minute perf deep-dive for next week.
[07:02] Avery: I'll upload the security pack and onboarding playbook, and post links in CRM. I'll also send calendar invites for the perf session after Miguel proposes times.
[07:11] Tom: We'll get infra diagram and PII list across by tomorrow EOD.
[07:15] Priya: We'll confirm peering window and our Okta contact.
[07:18] Derek: I'll send the k8s cluster details and expected QPS.
[07:21] Miguel: Cool. Anything else on the technical front?
[07:24] Tom: Not for now, thanks.
[07:26] [some crosstalk / background]
[07:30] Avery: Great. We'll follow up with the doc links and a proposed schedule. Thanks everyone — looking forward to getting the pilot rolling.
[07:38] Tom: Thanks, appreciate it.
[07:40] Priya: Thanks all.
[07:42] Derek: Bye.
[07:44] Miguel: Bye.
